title: Chartly whole-product workflow and UI blueprint
status: P00 design baseline explicitly accepted by the user on 2 November 2026. No production feature or adapter certification is implied.

modules.name: Workspace
modules.purpose: Manage environments; use the original chart and independent journal books for actual trading, practice and review.
modules.boundary: Chart and Journal are focused destinations. Open manages the environment through Overview, Connections and Settings.

screens.name: Workspace home and environments
layout: Keep the current profile cards and Chart / Journal / Open actions.
Show Live, Paper or journal-only intent, source readiness and the relevant book/account identity.
Keep Combined Analysis as an explicit cross-portfolio action.
actions: Open Chart, Journal or portfolio management
screens.gap: Manual journal entry into the product and truthful live/paper readiness are not complete.

screens.name: Create an environment or standalone book
screens.base: Existing New profile dialog; current persisted types are live/replay
layout: Keep the existing creation dialog styling.
Offer the user jobs: Journal only, Paper/replay, or Connected trading.
Ask only for the book, account or dataset fields required by that job; show what will actually be created.
actions: Create a manual book without a broker
screens.gap: Journal-only is a required first-use path, not currently a distinct persisted profile type. Define migration before changing ownership.

screens.name: Open: portfolio/environment management
layout: Overview: identity, account/book, observed balances, readiness and running-task shortcuts.
Connections: this environment’s data/account/terminal bindings.
Settings: defaults, timezone, limits and archive; Chart and Journal remain shortcuts out of management.
actions: Open the existing chart or book
screens.gap: The navigation separation is implemented; readiness and balance labels still need to be backed by observed scoped data.

screens.name: Original chart terminal
layout: Keep the existing toolbar, chart grid, drawings, watchlist, indicator controls, right rail and bottom dock.
Add source/account/mode/readiness and instrument context within the existing controls.
Use contextual links to Fundamentals, journal evidence and a Strategy Builder project.
actions: Apply a built-in or validated custom indicator
Open research, log/review a trade, or inspect a report’s trade
screens.gap: The terminal exists. Research, dataset, project revision and book handoffs are not all connected; opening the chart must not start a bot.

screens.name: Orders, positions and execution context
layout: Keep the existing order/position/trade views and chart-side order tools.
Show the actual selected account, demo/live state, connection health and command outcome.
Present risk, sizing, protective-order support and copying destinations only when supported.
actions: Inspect working orders and confirmed fills
screens.gap: The dock currently uses legacy global broker/app mode. Profile labels do not establish per-account execution authority. Multi-account execution/copying requires later verified contracts.

screens.name: Paper/replay setup and run library
screens.base: TraderReplay.tsx and profile Overview run shortcuts
layout: Keep existing run cards/creation controls; distinguish manual replay from automated testing.
Select a real saved dataset, instrument, range, timezone, starting balance and simulation costs.
Show coverage errors, warmup and resume/checkpoint status before enabling Start.
actions: Resume or inspect an existing run
screens.gap: Current run creation stores a source description and Draft state. It does not prove a dataset-bound persistent paper ledger.

screens.name: Paper session in the original chart
screens.surface: Original chart replay controls + session summary
layout: Keep chart presentation and replay controls.
Make the simulation clock, available data, paper orders/positions and session book visible.
Show completed-run results and restart/resume behavior.
screens.gap: Visual replay exists; deterministic paper fills, durable session/account state and once-only journal ingestion need an integrated verification journey.

screens.name: Independent journal books and book setup
screens.base: Existing profile Journal actions are the starting surface
layout: Each connected book names exactly one account; manual books have no external account binding.
Show book identity and source/sync coverage without requiring a chart or execution setup.
Open the existing journal presentation, not a new replacement ledger.
actions: Bind a connected book to one verified account
Import a statement or configure read-only sync
screens.gap: Current journal persistence is profile-scoped. A distinct durable book/account model and existing multi-destination migration are still required.

screens.name: Journal review workspace
layout: Preserve Overview, Trades, Calendar, Breakdown and optional Mind.
Keep book identity, filters, trade details, notes and performance charts.
Add source/coverage and review actions in the existing hierarchy; keep portfolio management behind Open.
actions: Log, edit or close a trade
screens.gap: Separation and chart/management return filters are tested. Complete book ownership, source reconciliation and the full trade lifecycle remain unfinished.

screens.name: Capture, edit, close and review a trade
layout: Lock the destination book/account and show timezone and asset-appropriate quantity units.
Keep open-trade facts separate from close facts and realized P&L.
Keep source facts separate from user notes, screenshots, setup tags and review choices.
actions: Save an open or completed manual trade
Edit/correct or close the same record
screens.gap: Manual creation/deletion and review fields exist; the data hook has no complete update/close lifecycle. Preserve drafts on save failure.

screens.name: Statement import and validation
screens.base: New flow beside existing Log trade; reuse journal components
layout: Choose a book/account, source file and timezone/units mapping.
Preview valid rows, row errors, duplicates, corrections and source coverage before commit.
Show a durable import result and reversible/recoverable correction path.
actions: Commit valid records or resolve issues
screens.gap: A market-candle CSV upload and journal CSV export are not a trade-statement import workflow.

screens.name: Read-only journal sync and reconciliation
screens.base: Profile Connections currently stores configuration only
layout: Show the account/source binding, history coverage, last successful sync and current job.
Show new/corrected records and ambiguous cross-source matches without discarding notes.
Provide retry, backfill/import and conflict resolution; cached journal remains readable offline.
actions: Connect a supported read-only history source
Sync while the local engine is running
Resolve gaps, duplicate candidates and corrections
screens.gap: Needs real adapters, cursors, account identity and canonical executions. A chart tab need not stay open; closing the local engine stops updates.

screens.name: Combined Analysis
layout: Keep selection, clear-all and explicit Save selection.
Keep currency groups and the same portfolio selection behind every displayed result.
Add coverage, duplicate-account/source protection and live/paper comparison rules as their contracts mature.
actions: Review selected metrics and return to an individual portfolio
screens.gap: Selection/empty/save behavior and selected-only results are tested. Canonical account deduplication, named comparison sets and broader analytics semantics remain separate work.

modules.name: Fundamentals
modules.purpose: Research companies and assets, inspect original evidence and carry decisions into charts and journal reviews.
modules.boundary: Research is usable without an execution account. Company facts, quotes, macro data and relationship intelligence each need verified source coverage.

screens.name: Research home, search and saved lists
screens.surface: New research page using existing app components
screens.base: /fundamentals now has an availability notice; company search/source service is not implemented
layout: Search company/asset names with issuer/listing disambiguation.
Show saved lists and recently researched entities.
Expose supported coverage and source availability rather than a fake populated dashboard.
screens.gap: A direct navigation destination now exists; the functional research workflow is absent. Yahoo is a source candidate, not a connected certified provider.

screens.name: Company/asset overview
layout: Header: issuer and selected listing, source, as-of time and freshness.
Center: sourced business description and supported headline facts; asset-specific layouts later.
Tabs: Statements, Metrics, Reports, Events and later Relationships; explicit Chart and Save research actions.
actions: Change listing without changing issuer facts
screens.gap: No fundamentals data model or page exists. Missing fields stay unavailable; fetching current facts does not make them historical backtest inputs.

screens.name: Financial statements
screens.base: New Income / Balance Sheet / Cash Flow views
layout: Annual/quarterly periods, fiscal labels, units, scaling and currency.
Reported values with source drilldown and missing-cell explanations.
Restated versus as-reported selection only when supported by stored revisions.
screens.gap: Normalization and report provenance are absent; duration and instant facts must not be treated interchangeably.

screens.name: Metrics, valuation and comparison definitions
layout: Supported reported/calculated ratios and growth with formula definitions.
Period, price timestamp, currency and input citations for each calculation.
Unavailable denominators, negative earnings and unsupported TTM shown honestly.
screens.gap: Do not populate attractive metric tiles until their source/period/formula tests pass.

screens.name: Filings, original reports and source detail
screens.base: New report index and fact-source panel
layout: Document type, publication time, provider and original link.
Fact-to-document references and revision/amendment context.
Freshness, unavailable documents and refresh failure recovery.
screens.gap: An overview feed alone may not supply original filings. Verify report access separately rather than inventing citations.

screens.name: Earnings and corporate events
layout: Dated earnings, dividends, splits and relevant announcements where covered.
Separate announced/estimated/confirmed events and display source/timezone.
Link to reports, chart timestamps and saved notes.
screens.gap: Events and estimates need their own coverage and revision contract; no universal calendar exists.

screens.name: Screener and company comparison
layout: A declared supported universe and consistent metric/period filters.
Side-by-side facts with source, currency and missing-value treatment.
Saved criteria and explicit inclusion; avoid an opaque universal quality score.
screens.gap: Needs normalized facts and real universe coverage before the screening UI can make truthful comparisons.

screens.name: Saved research and decision notebook
screens.base: New local research records; references into existing journal
layout: Notes, thesis, linked entities, reports and captured facts with source dates.
Distinguish saved evidence from refreshed current data.
Choose the destination book/trade/note when attaching research.
actions: Attach a citation to a journal review
Return to the exact researched company or chart
screens.gap: There is no durable research notebook/snapshot workflow. A research note never creates a trade fill.

screens.name: Company relationships
layout: Supplier/customer/ownership edges with type, source, date and evidence.
Inspect relationships without treating inference as reported fact.
Show changes over time and distinguish verified relationships from unavailable coverage.
screens.gap: This is part of the Bloomberg-like vision. A company overview source does not establish a complete customer/supplier graph.

screens.name: Market intelligence, economic calendar and reports
layout: Supported macro series, economic releases and original economic reports.
Release time, observation period, revisions, source and freshness; original links for any licensed news/report coverage.
Watchlists, dated events and chart overlays only where their data is supported.
actions: Inspect a macro series or release
Save research or configure a supported reminder
screens.gap: Price history alone supplies neither macro fundamentals nor news. Each dataset and calendar needs a source, coverage and revision contract.

screens.name: Asset-specific fundamentals
screens.surface: Asset pages with distinct data models
screens.base: New crypto / fund / FX-rates / futures research increments
layout: Crypto: supply, issuance/unlocks and supported network/funding data with methodology.
Funds: holdings, NAV and distributions; FX/rates: relevant economic series and rate context.
Futures: contract, expiry/roll and term structure. Retain source, date, units and missing-data rules throughout.
actions: Open the matching original chart or cited research
screens.gap: Universal architecture does not make one company-ratio template suitable for every asset class. Verify and release each asset model separately.

modules.name: Strategy Builder
modules.purpose: Create indicators or executable strategies, test them, inspect evidence and deliberately apply validated work to charts or paper environments.
modules.boundary: Indicator and Strategy are the two artifact kinds. A bot is a deployment of a strategy revision. Backtests, optimization trials and real trades remain different records.

screens.name: Project library
screens.base: /strategy-builder currently says the new builder is unavailable
layout: Create Indicator or Create Strategy; search and reopen saved projects.
Show drafts, validated revisions, parameter sets and latest experiment.
Import/export, duplicate and archive without exposing legacy tool hosts.
screens.gap: The old launchers were removed. A new project library is not implemented.

screens.name: Indicator/strategy authoring
screens.base: Existing ScriptPanel, compiler and source store are reuse points
layout: Left: project files/dependencies; center: code or supported visual rules.
Right: typed parameters, plots and strategy settings; bottom: diagnostics/preview.
Draft/revision status and save/conflict recovery. Keep chart-side editing linked to the same project.
actions: Preview an indicator or define executable strategy rules
screens.gap: Current chart scripts are not a durable versioned project/dependency library. Arbitrary code need not round-trip into visual blocks.

screens.name: Indicator preview and validation
screens.base: Existing custom indicator registration and chart application
layout: Selected dataset, typed inputs, overlay/pane outputs and reference values.
Warmup, missing bars, higher-timeframe availability and repaint behavior.
Show validation outcome and exact revision/parameters.
actions: Apply to an original chart or use in a strategy
screens.gap: An indicator has no trading P&L on its own. Add explicit strategy rules before performance testing.

screens.name: Strategy rules and trading assumptions
layout: Entry/exit conditions, indicator dependencies, sizing, stops/targets and session rules.
Bar-close/next-open timing and supported fill policy.
Instrument economics, cost assumptions and clear validation errors.
actions: Build supported visual rules or code
screens.gap: A configurable collection of indicators is not yet an executable strategy.

screens.name: Backtest setup and experiment jobs
layout: Pin revision, parameters, instrument, dataset version, range and warmup.
Set costs, fill assumptions and resource budget.
Show queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled/interrupted states and recovery.
actions: Reopen its report after leaving the chart
screens.gap: The reusable chart-bound engine is not a standalone offline dataset/job/report product.

screens.name: Saved performance report and trade drilldown
layout: Overview/assumptions, equity/drawdown, trades, costs/exposure, breakdowns and diagnostics.
Exact manifest, dataset range, engine and revision identity.
Click a simulated trade to inspect its original-chart context; return to the same report.
actions: Compare or start a bounded validation study
screens.gap: Current inspected result state is chart component state; durable reproducible reports and complete metric definitions are missing.

screens.name: Parameter optimization and candidate ledger
screens.base: New builder study workflow; reuse validated run engine
layout: Parameter ranges/constraints, trial estimate and budget.
Every candidate, rejection/failure and scoring objective.
Performance/drawdown/cost/sample-size tradeoffs and parameter stability.
actions: Save a parameter set against its exact revision
screens.gap: Existing parameter inputs and portfolio allocation analytics do not implement strategy optimization.

screens.name: Out-of-sample and stress testing
screens.base: P21 robustness work; existing pieces have narrower scope
layout: Chronological train/validation/holdout and walk-forward definitions.
Supported cost/slippage/latency/market-period stresses and seeded resampling.
Scenario assumptions, degradation, failures and absolute results; distinguish execution reruns from return transformations.
screens.gap: No complete arbitrary-strategy stress/walk-forward product exists; do not relabel fixed-allocation analytics as one.

screens.name: Compare, save and promote a candidate
layout: Compare revision, data, costs and trial conditions before ranking.
Save a selected parameter set and the researcher’s explanation.
Separate Apply indicator, Inspect trades, Create paper run and Prepare bot deployment actions.
actions: Apply a validated indicator to a chosen chart
Test a strategy in a paper environment
screens.gap: Promotion is explicit and reversible at draft stage. A good backtest never grants live execution permission.

modules.name: Workflows
modules.purpose: Automate repeatable tasks and operate their runs with explicit scope, logs and recovery.
modules.boundary: Keep Flow. It orchestrates triggers and actions; it is not an indicator editor or a substitute strategy tester.

screens.name: Workflow library and useful templates
layout: Keep saved workflow cards, import/export and active/draft state.
Group supported templates by user job: alerts, data refresh, reports and eligible trading actions.
Show bound environment/account and last run without claiming unsupported actions are ready.
screens.gap: The engine/list exists. Research refresh and journal-sync templates require real underlying actions.

screens.name: Visual automation builder
layout: Keep node palette, graph canvas, node settings and execution logs.
Define trigger, inputs, conditions, action capabilities and target scope.
Link supported saved project/jobs instead of copying strategy code into another engine.
screens.gap: Existing global user/API-key binding must evolve into explicit environment/account/project revision bindings.

screens.name: Test, permissions and activation
screens.base: Existing Flow validation and lifecycle guards are reuse points
layout: Show resolved account/environment, exact action permissions and expected effects.
Separate read-only preview from real action execution.
Make schedules, webhook credentials, approvals and activation status clear.
screens.gap: A generic Play button cannot hide execution authority or pretend an unimplemented read-only preview is a dry run.

screens.name: Runs, logs, approvals and recovery
screens.base: Flow run logs and ActionCenter are reuse points
layout: Trigger, scope, each step’s result, outputs and timestamps.

screens.gap: Need one visible execution history with step outcomes. Retrying an unknown trading submission must not duplicate an order.

screens.name: Strategy bot deployments and operations
screens.surface: Runtime/deployment detail; linked from profile and builder
screens.base: Existing StrategiesPanel / OpenScript deployment and runner services
layout: Frozen strategy revision, parameters, instrument/source and paper/demo/live account.

actions: Prepare a deployment from a candidate
Inspect its account activity and journal
screens.gap: User-confirmed navigation home: Workflows → Deployments, with contextual Builder/profile/chart links. This is a separate runtime type, not a Flow graph. Existing runtimes and scheduler dependencies must be migrated safely.

modules.boundary: These are dialogs, drawers or shared pages reached from the user’s current task. They are not another top-level Tools directory.

screens.surface: Shared activity drawer / linked job details
screens.base: Reuse Historify jobs, Flow logs, diagnostics; unify ownership
layout: Scoped queued/running/failed/stale work with last successful outcome.
Source/account/book/project/run identity and a route to the owning section.
Progress, supported cancel/retry, interrupted recovery and actionable notifications.

screens.base: Existing journal CSV export and backend databases are incomplete pieces

Include books, environments, chart layouts, research, projects and results under a defined policy.
screens.gap: A filtered trade CSV is not a complete backup. Durable ownership and migration rules are foundational P01/P02 work.

journeys.name: Journal only: record and improve trading done elsewhere
journeys.outcome: A manual book is useful without chart data, a broker connection, bots or AI. Chart drilldown is optional.

journeys.name: Connected journal: import, catch up and reconcile
journeys.outcome: One account’s source observations reconcile into its book; duplicate candidates and corrections preserve user notes. Statement import is an alternative initial source or a backfill when needed.

journeys.name: Discretionary paper/replay: learn from saved history
journeys.outcome: The original chart runs a dataset-bound paper session, saves its fills once and resumes after restart.

journeys.name: Build an indicator and use it on the original chart
journeys.outcome: An exact validated indicator revision and parameter set attach to the chosen chart without submitting orders.

journeys.name: Build, test, stress and paper-validate a strategy
journeys.outcome: The candidate has saved reproducible evidence; research trials stay outside real-account journal P&L. Parameter search is a separate optional study, not a mandatory way to manufacture a winner.

journeys.name: Research a company and retain the decision evidence
journeys.outcome: Research is useful on its own. Optional chart and journal links retain the decision evidence; unsupported company relationships remain unavailable.

journeys.name: Automate a supported task and recover failures
journeys.outcome: The task runs with explicit capabilities, visible outcomes and supported recovery; activation never invents missing actions.

journeys.name: Connected discretionary trading
journeys.outcome: Eligible account-specific fills reach their own books. No strategy project or bot is required. Copying follows verified single-account execution.

journeys.name: Prepare and operate an account-bound strategy bot
journeys.outcome: A strategy candidate becomes a separately configured deployment after capability and account/risk checks. The chart is an optional view; it does not control the runtime lifetime.

rules: Preserve the original chart and journal presentation. Add workflow context and missing behavior in those screens.
A profile/portfolio is an environment inside Workspace; a journal book is a record owner; an account is an external or simulated identity. They are not aliases.
Each connected book belongs to exactly one account; manual records use separate books. Copy destinations each journal their own account fills.
Users may use just journal, chart, paper trading, strategy research or fundamentals. Optional modules cannot impose unrelated broker or AI setup.
Market data, account-history access and execution permission are separate. Saved configuration is not observed health.
Manual replay, automated backtests, optimization trials and running bots have separate lifecycles and records.
A saved research/project/report revision is not rewritten when newer data or code arrives.
Closing a chart changes a view, not a running bot or local sync destination. Closing the local engine stops local workers unless a separate background service is explicitly enabled.
All cross-section links carry authoritative entity/account/book/dataset/revision context and preserve the return location. Unsupported mapping gets a recovery action, not a default ticker.
No feature or P00 milestone is complete merely because a route, tab, form, backend utility or review screen exists.
gaps: The journal UI is good, but it is still profile-scoped persistence; the independent book model and migration rules are unfinished.
Open/edit/close/correct, statement import, read-only sync and annotation-preserving reconciliation need connected screens and backend behavior.
Saved candles, exact instrument identity, version/coverage and a durable simulated account must connect to the original chart.
A library, editor, saved experiments/reports, parameter studies, robustness and candidate handoff are absent as one product despite reusable engines.
Search, company pages, statements, reports, research notes and sourced relationships have no complete implementation.
Existing chart dock and Flow resolve legacy global contexts; portfolio configuration does not establish per-account authority or copying.
Books, chart layouts, sources, research, projects, jobs/results and backups need coherent ownership and restore guarantees.
Every screen needs useful first-use, pending, partial, error, stale, offline, permission and return paths; missing controls must lead to recovery.
decisions: User-confirmed primary tab order: Workspace, Fundamentals, Strategy Builder, Workflows. All four remain directly visible; Settings and shared resources stay contextual.
Use the current Chart / Journal / Open model. Add a first-use Journal only job without forcing it to be a live trading account.
Start Fundamentals with sourced company overview, statements and original reports; treat relationship intelligence and other asset classes as staged expansions.
User-confirmed runtime placement: Workflows → Deployments, linked from a strategy candidate, profile Overview and chart. A deployment is not converted into a Flow graph.

Apply the confirmed one-active-connected-book/account rule and conservative legacy classification in P00_DECISIONS. P01/P02 implement identity, migration and chart-workspace association contracts without guessing old record ownership.
